facts.claim: IEM serves the NWS warning archive through one CGI with a format switch
facts.value: Endpoint /cgi-bin/request/gis/watchwarn.py. accept=csv or accept=shapefile (the form also offers Excel and KML). timeopt=1: events whose start falls between start and end; timeopt=2: events valid at one UTC time. Phenomenon and significance filters apply only with limitps=1; addsvs=1 adds follow-up polygon rows (CON, EXP, COR); CAN rows are county type with no polygon.
facts.evidence: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/request/gis/watchwarn.phtml (HTTP 200, 83154 B); form controls read.
facts.refuted_by: CAN rows are county type (gtype C) with no polygon in addsvs output (June 2025: 129). Only CON, EXP and COR add polygon rows.
facts.corrected_from: addsvs=1 adds follow-up polygons (CON, EXP, COR, CAN rows).

facts.claim: The phenomenon filter is not applied unless limitps=1
facts.value: TO-only request without limitps for 2008 to 2026 returned 105765 rows with 34 phenomenon codes (SV 25411 rows, TO 888 rows, WW 20865 rows among them).
facts.evidence: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/gis/watchwarn.py?simple=1&location_group=states&states%5B%5D=MT&timeopt=1&year1=2008&month1=1&day1=1&hour1=0&minute1=0&year2=2026&month2=10&day2=17&hour2=23&minute2=59&phenomena%5B%5D=TO&significance%5B%5D=W&accept=csv (HTTP 200, 19678899 B); counted from the CSV.

facts.claim: Two phenomena in one request return only the first phenomenon's rows
facts.value: June 2025, Montana, SV and TO requested together with limitps=1 (issuance output): 616 rows, phenomena {'SV': 616}. A TO-only request returns TO rows. The archive pulls therefore request SV and TO in separate calls; the earlier combined pull was not used for TO.
facts.evidence: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/cgi-bin/request/gis/watchwarn.py?accept=csv&simple=1&location_group=states&states%5B%5D=MT&timeopt=1&year1=2025&month1=6&day1=1&hour1=0&minute1=0&year2=2025&month2=6&day2=30&hour2=23&minute2=59&phenomena%5B%5D=SV&phenomena%5B%5D=TO&significance%5B%5D=W&limitps=1 (HTTP 200, 120866 B).

facts.claim: IEM tag numbers agree with the official text in all sampled products
facts.value: 66 official products (2010 to 2026; 3 before 2014; 55 sampled and 11 picked) were read as text. IEM hailtag, windtag, tornadotag and damagetag agree with the text tag lines in 66 of 66 products (0 disagreements). The text has a '<' qualifier on 13 hail lines and 6 wind lines; IEM stores the number without the '<'.
facts.evidence: Official text via https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/nwstext/{product_id} (see the nwstext rows in urls_checked); comparison script tagcheck2.py.

facts.claim: Text tag wording (examples, quoted)
facts.value: 2025 product: 'MAX WIND GUST...<50 MPH' (IEM windtag 50.0, a '<' value). 2026 product: 'MAX HAIL SIZE...<.75 IN' (IEM hailtag 0.75, a '<' value). 2014 product: 'HAIL...1.00IN' and 'WIND...60MPH' (IEM 1.0 and 60.0). 2021 product: 'HAIL THREAT...RADAR INDICATED' and 'THUNDERSTORM DAMAGE THREAT...CONSIDERABLE'; IEM damagetag CONSIDERABLE. 2024 tornado product: 'TORNADO...OBSERVED'. 2012 product has no HAIL, WIND or THREAT tag lines; all four IEM fields are empty.
facts.evidence: nwstext rows in urls_checked (product IDs listed there).

facts.claim: Source of the threat (radar or observed) is not in the IEM tag fields
facts.value: The text has lines such as 'HAIL THREAT...RADAR INDICATED' and 'WIND THREAT...OBSERVED'. The shapefile and CSV carry numeric hail and wind tags and TORNTAG (POSSIBLE on SV events; OBSERVED or RADAR INDICATED on TO events). The radar or observed source of the hail and wind threat is not a field in either export.
facts.evidence: Shapefile DBF field list (fact on fields) and nwstext rows.

facts.claim: IEM API sbw_interval limits and parameters
facts.value: At most three wfo values per call: 422 body 'List should have at most 3 items after validation, not 4'. fmt must be json, geojson or txt: csv gives 422 'Input should be 'json', 'geojson' or 'txt''. OpenAPI: begints is the inclusive window start for issuance, endts the exclusive end; only_new defaults to true; the default is the issuance geometry ('The default option is to only provide the issuance geometry.'). Rate-limit wording found in the OpenAPI document: 0 matches.
facts.evidence: https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/vtec/sbw_interval.geojson?begints=2025-06-15T00:00:00Z&endts=2025-06-16T00:00:00Z&ph=SV&ph=TO&wfo=BYZ&wfo=TFX&wfo=GGW&wfo=MSO (HTTP 422, 214 B); https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/vtec/sbw_interval.csv?begints=2025-06-15T00:00:00Z&endts=2025-06-16T00:00:00Z&ph=SV&wfo=TFX (HTTP 422, 162 B); https://mesonet.agron.iastate.edu/api/1/openapi.json (HTTP 200, 120597 B).

terms.ncei: Not accessed. The NWS API page names NCEI as the route to an official CAP archive; NCEI access terms were not read.
terms.attribution: The IEM disclaimer asks for attribution to the Iowa Environmental Mesonet of Iowa State University; the NWS page asks that data not be presented as official government material when modified. Both quotes above.
terms.personal_data: Warning polygons carry no addresses or owner names. No address or owner data was used in this workstream.

limits: Scope is warnings only: SV and TO, significance W, Montana through IEM's states filter. Watches, advisories, statements, marine and flood products are not included.

The IEM archive is a secondary copy of NWS products. Completeness was tested only by sampling (66 official texts, one office-day API comparison); no full comparison with an NWS-side archive was made because the NWS page points to NCEI and NCEI was not accessed.

Numeric tags drop the '<' qualifier: 13 of 61 products with a numeric hail value and 6 of 56 with a numeric wind value have '<' (review recount). A tag value in the IEM fields is an upper bound where the text says '<'.
Tag sparsity before 2014: hail tags present on 84/543 (2010), 64/481 (2011), 34/278 (2012) and 73/588 (2013) SV events (count/total); only three official texts from those years were read.
Tags describe the NWS product's stated hazard, not measured hail or wind at a location. Polygon coverage is not evidence of hail or damage.
Coverage uses warning polygons as issued or updated, not clipped to the state line (see the coverage fact for the box west of Montana).
EXP rows are excluded from coverage. The rule 'an event ends at its last NEW, CON or COR polygon' is an engineering choice, not checked against NWS VTEC directive wording.
No county-only (UGC) events were found for SV or TO in 2008 to 2026, so the county-code fallback named in AGENTS.md rule 6 is not exercised by this archive.
Office coverage: the states filter returns rows from BIS, UNR, RIW, OTX and PIH (polygons with a Montana zone). They are kept and labelled by office.
The Benchland check is one point and one event day; the 15 km test uses 300 random points, not the MRMS grid. SPC and LSR times were compared in review (see the Benchland report-time fact).
The random coverage shares use fixed seeds and a bounding box; they are descriptive, not estimates of the state's area.
Time: all times UTC (IEM CSV and shapefile fields, EXPIRED, POLY_BEG, POLY_END). NWS API timestamps include offsets such as -06:00.

Skipped: NCEI archive (no request); NWS GIS shapefile archives; text fetch for all 2,240 SV polygon events (66 sampled); years before 2008 (the form offers from 1986); watches; the offline lookup is a prototype outside the repository and is not committed.
The 2021 window starts 2021-10-17; 2026 runs to 2026-10-17 23:59 UTC, so the window is partial for 2026.
open_questions: VTEC: NWS asks for comment on discontinuing VTEC and moving to CAP as the primary format (quoted). If that happens, how will the IEM archive and ETN-based event keys carry forward? Timeline not found.
NCEI: is there a complete, public NWS CAP archive with polygons and tags for 2021 to 2026, and on what terms? Not checked.

Licence: the IEM disclaimer says the materials are in the public domain and asks for attribution; the IEM footer carries a copyright line. Which reading applies for redistribution in a product? (W10.)

Qualifier loss: should each warning's official text be fetched and stored to keep '<' values? About 2,257 SV and TO NEW products for five years; text size about 1.1 to 2.2 KB each (roughly 2.5 to 5 MB in total). Decide in W9.
Tags before 2014 are sparse (hail on 12.2 to 15.5 percent of SV events in 2010 to 2013; 84/543 = 15.5%). Is the absence a missing tag or no hazard stated? Needs more text samples from those years.
Geometry rule: should a per-address statement use the issuance polygon, the latest polygon, or every polygon in effect at the time? Affects counts in the coverage fact. (W10.)
EXP rule: confirm with NWS VTEC wording that an EXP product ends the event at its issuance time, and that the POLY_END in EXP rows is the scheduled expiry.

Completeness of the states filter for Montana polygons from offices outside the four Montana WFOs (for example BIS, UNR, RIW, OTX and PIH, which appear in the results) was not tested against NWS zone lists.

Benchland 2025-06-15: no Montana polygon covered the point or its 15 km circle at 22:30 or 23:12 UTC in this archive. Reviewed: SPC and LSR Benchland reports are at 20:05, 20:10 and 20:20 UTC, not 22:30 or 23:12; the first two were inside polygons, the third outside all polygons while a warning was in effect.
NWS API says the User-Agent approach 'will be replaced with an API key in the future' (quoted). Access terms may change.

Bulk access: no rate-limit or fair-use text was found for the IEM API or CGI. The archive pulls used one request at a time with a 0.3 to 0.4 second pause. Confirm with the IEM before automated nightly use. The form limits a download to one year when no state or WFO filter is set.
EXP rule: the ETN 48 EXP polygon (21:51 to 22:00 UTC, 2025-06-15) covers Benchland, so skipping EXP rows leaves that interval uncovered; decide the rule before W10 wording.
